definitions.explanation: Not quickly. Taking one's time to do something.
In a relaxed manner without hurrying.

examples.japanese: ゆっくり{話|はな}してください。
ゆっくり{食|た}べましょう。
もう{少|すこ}しゆっくり{読|よ}んでもらえますか。{分|わ}かりませんでした。
examples.english: Could you read a bit more slowly? I didn't understand.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}が{暗|くら}いから、ゆっくり{運転|うんてん}してください。{急|いそ}がなくてもいいです。
examples.english: The road is dark, so please drive slowly. You don't need to hurry.

examples.japanese: ゆっくり{休|やす}んでください。
examples.english: Please take it easy and rest.

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}はゆっくりできた?
examples.english: Were you able to relax on the weekend?

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}でゆっくりしたいから、{予定|よてい}は{少|すく}なくしました。
examples.english: I want to relax on the trip, so I reduced my plans.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{仕事|しごと}が{休|やす}みなので、{家|いえ}でゆっくり{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むつもりです。
examples.english: I have the day off work today, so I plan to relax at home and read a book.

notes: Always written in hiragana. One of the most useful words for asking someone to slow down. ゆっくり{休|やす}んでください is a common phrase wishing someone to rest well. Can also be used as a na-adjective: ゆっくりな{時間|じかん} (leisurely time).
